verdict.rationale: OpenAI's speech-to-text docs describe uploading a completed recording to get a final transcript, and they publish a 25 MB file limit and the accepted formats, including video containers mp4 and webm. A documented CLI call (`audio:transcriptions create --file /path/to/file/audio.mp3`) shows a local file being submitted to the transcriptions API. Missing for 10: the raw HTTP endpoint path or request schema is not shown in the evidence (the OpenAPI probes returned 404), and there is no independent or hands-on corroboration of the hosted API upload flow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can submit a local audio or video file for transcription through a documented API endpoint, with accepted formats and size limits published

citations.quote: Upload the audio and receive a final transcript
Files can be up to 25 MB. Supported input formats are `mp3`, `mp4`, `mpeg`, `mpga`, `m4a`, `wav`, and `webm`.
